subject: Hosted API tiering and cloud-displacement plan for BrightApps
messages:
From: Emma Liao <emma@brightapps.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluating Redwood as a drop-in for our cloud endpoints

Hi Lauren,

Quick note from BrightApps — we're evaluating replacements for our current OpenAI/Anthropic hosted endpoints for user-facing generation. Two items that will determine whether we can move forward: (1) a competitive per-token economics model under a usage-based / monthly commit structure, and (2) a clear operational plan for routing/fallback so we don't regress latency or quality during high volume windows.

Can you share a concise breakdown of how Redwood would price for a hosted usage profile like ours (expected ~8–12M generated tokens/month initially, scaling to ~40M within 6 months)? Specifically:
- What discounting do you offer across commit tiers?
- Do you support temporary pilot pricing that rolls into commits?
- Is there a written commitment/guarantee you can provide if we claim you're matching a competitor's published price?

Also, procurement will need SOC 2 + export controls info; we can share a questionnaire after we see a pricing sketch.

Thanks — can we get a short call tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Emma
Emma Liao
Head of Platform, BrightApps
emma@brightapps.com

---
Attachment: n/a

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liao <emma@brightapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-12T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood as a drop-in for our cloud endpoints

Emma — thanks for the clear ask and context. Short answer: yes, we can provide a tiered, usage-based program with a pilot path and contractual language to address competitive matching / displacement. High level below and I've attached a one-page proposal to start.

Summary (short):
- Pilot: 3-week trial with usage credit. Pilot rate (listed): $0.0009/token for generation traffic; usage credit applied to first committed month if you convert.
- Commit tiers (monthly committed tokens, example rates):
  * 0–10M tokens: $0.00085/token
  * 10–50M tokens: $0.00065/token
  * 50M+: custom enterprise pricing (contact for block pricing)
  These are illustrative; we can blend to match target effective rate depending on token mix.
- Competitive match / displacement: we can include a 'price parity' clause in the SOW that adjusts the blended rate if BrightApps provides verifiable public pricing from OpenAI/Anthropic (we treat published list as the comparator). We do require a minimum commit window (3 months) for parity guarantees.
- Operational routing: Redwood supports model-fallback policies and per-route routing. For example, route high-importance traffic to a premium variant and overflow to a lower-cost quantized variant automatically when capacity or cost thresholds trigger — this preserves latency SLAs while managing unit economics.

I've attached a short pricing proposal (redwood-pricing-proposal.pdf) and a sample SOW for the pilot (pilot-sow.docx). Procurement asks (SOC 2 etc.) — we can share our compliance pack after NDA/procurement request.

If this looks directionally right, I can put together a firm offer and run a quick internal approval for a one-off pilot discount if you need a lower trial rate. Call? I have 3–4pm PT today.

—Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com

---
Attachments: redwood-pricing-proposal.pdf; pilot-sow.docx

From: Emma Liao <emma@brightapps.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T09:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood as a drop-in for our cloud endpoints

Thanks Lauren — the structure helps. A couple of follow-ups so we can fast-track procurement: 
1) For the pilot, can you do a 3-week trial at $0.0006/token with up to 10M tokens and a $2k minimum commitment? BrightApps will commit to convert to a monthly committed plan if performance/latency meets SLA within the pilot.
2) For price parity: procurement prefers a contractual clause that ties effective blended rate to an explicit comparator (OpenAI text-gen gpt-4.1x or Anthropic equivalent). We'll share the public rate we want matched.
3) Can you send the SOC 2 cert or a link to your security pack for our vendor team to begin the questionnaire?

If we can agree to the pilot number and a short parity clause, procurement can raise an initial PO quickly.

Emma

Attachment: procurement@brightapps.com (procurement contact)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: BrightApps pilot ask — approval for one-off trial discount?

Ben / Vivek — forwarding BrightApps' asks. They want a 3-week pilot at $0.0006/token up to 10M tokens with a $2k minimum and a conversion commitment if SLA is met. Procurement also wants a parity clause that references public competitor pricing.

I've attached our internal cost model for a quick look (internal-cost-model.xlsx). My recommendation: approve a capped pilot discount that converts to a 3-month minimum commit at a blended break-even rate; if they convert, apply a 10% conversion credit against the first committed month.

Suggested approved language: 
- Pilot: 3 weeks, capped at 10M tokens, trial rate $0.0007/token (compromise), $2k minimum.
- Conversion: if BrightApps signs a 3-month commit within 30 days of pilot end, apply credit equal to pilot spend up to 50% of first month.
- Parity: include an audit-and-adjust mechanism referencing public list prices; parity applies only to materially-comparable endpoints and excludes ephemeral promotional pricing.

Need an approval by EOD today to get them a PO. Thoughts?

—Lauren

---
Attachment: internal-cost-model.xlsx

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-13T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: BrightApps pilot ask — approval for one-off trial discount?

Lauren — agree we should be flexible but protect margin. Approve pilot at $0.0007/token up to 10M tokens with the $2k minimum. Firm conversion terms as you suggested but change conversion credit to 25% of pilot spend (not 50%). For parity language: legal to draft narrow comparator definition and allow us to exclude transient promotional rates. Also require that BrightApps provides the comparator link and screenshots if they invoke parity post-conversion.

Ben — please prepare the short SOW with those terms and get legal looped (cc'ing me).

Vivek
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liao <emma@brightapps.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-15T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating Redwood as a drop-in for our cloud endpoints

Emma — good news. We can approve a pilot with the following confirmed terms: 
- Pilot term: 3 weeks; trial rate: $0.0007/token; cap: 10M tokens; minimum billing: $2,000.
- Conversion: if BrightApps signs a 3-month commit within 30 days of pilot end, Redwood will credit 25% of pilot spend toward the first committed month.
- Parity: we will include a parity clause in the SOW that references public list prices; legal will draft narrow comparator and exclude short-term promotions. BrightApps will need to provide the comparator link and date if parity is invoked.

Attached: pilot SOW and the pricing one-pager (redwood-pricing-proposal.pdf; pilot-sow.docx). For procurement, we'll send our SOC 2 pack via secure link once an NDA or vendor request is received.

Next steps: if that looks good, confirm billing contact and a desired pilot start date and I'll send the SOW/DocuSign link. We can start as early as next Monday.

Thanks — looking forward to it.

—Lauren
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
lauren_bishop@redwood.com
